Leaf Scorch.description: Leaf scorch caused by high temperature or nutrient deficiency, leading to browning of leaf edges.
Leaf Scorch.treatment_organic: Mulch around the base to retain moisture. Apply compost tea.
Leaf Scorch.treatment_chemical: Apply balanced NPK fertilizer if nutrient deficiency is confirmed. Use anti-transpirants.
Leaf Scorch.prevention: Maintain adequate watering schedule. Provide shade during peak heat.

Reduced Zinc Absorption.description: Inability of the plant to absorb Zinc, possibly due to high soil pH or high Phosphorus levels.
Reduced Zinc Absorption.treatment_organic: Apply manure or compost to lower pH slightly and improve biological activity.
Reduced Zinc Absorption.treatment_chemical: Apply Zinc Sulphate (ZnSO4) foliar spray or soil application.
Reduced Zinc Absorption.prevention: monitor soil pH. Avoid excessive Phosphorus application.

Nutrient Imbalance.description: General imbalance of NPK or micronutrients preventing optimal growth.
Nutrient Imbalance.treatment_organic: Apply vermicompost or well-rotted cow dung.
Nutrient Imbalance.treatment_chemical: Use a balanced NPK fertilizer (e.g., 10-10-10) based on soil test.
Nutrient Imbalance.prevention: Regular soil testing and balanced fertilization.

Acidic Soil Stress.description: Soil pH is too low for the crop, leading to aluminum toxicity or nutrient unavailability.
Acidic Soil Stress.treatment_organic: Apply agricultural lime (calcium carbonate) or dolomite.
Acidic Soil Stress.treatment_chemical: Use liming materials. Avoid acidifying fertilizers (like Ammonium Sulfate).
Acidic Soil Stress.prevention: Regular pH testing. Use alkaline amendments if soil tends to be acidic.

Excess Vegetative Growth.description: Too much Nitrogen causing lush foliage but poor fruit/flower production.
Excess Vegetative Growth.treatment_organic: Stop applying manure. Add Carbon-rich material (sawdust) to tie up nitrogen.
Excess Vegetative Growth.treatment_chemical: Apply Phosphorus and Potassium to balance the ratio. Avoid Nitrogen fertilizers.
Excess Vegetative Growth.prevention: Follow recommended NPK ratios. Do not over-fertilize with Nitrogen.

Unknown Disease.description: An unidentified issue based on current parameters.
